findings.title: The required v1 manifest is again unresolved
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2 requires `prompts/resolved/prompt_manifest.resolved.v1.yaml` to contain exactly 13 activated prompts with valid inventory-derived boundaries.
findings.trigger: Criterion 2 is verified using its expressly prescribed v1 manifest path.
findings.consequence: Eleven downstream prompts are not activated and eight reference nonexistent filenames, so the required manifest cannot dispatch the execution set.
findings.evidence: The restored `prompt_manifest.resolved.v1.yaml` marks P01–P10/P02S as `template_requires_resolution` and uses invalid paths such as `P03_source_relocation.prompt.v3.yaml`. Checkpoint v4 relies instead on v2, but the criterion explicitly identifies v1 as the manifest to check.

findings.title: P02S still forbids the live structured-file edits assigned to it
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 4 requires P02S to be “assigned responsibility for all TOML/JSON/YAML edits” and to own all structured-file edits.
findings.trigger: P02S attempts to execute the pyproject, requirements, or CI workflow transformations assigned to it by manifest v2.
findings.consequence: Its prompt and authorized paths prohibit those live mutations, so P02S cannot perform or control the responsibility the manifest assigns.
findings.evidence: Manifest v2 assigns P02S `pyproject_toml_identity_updates`, `requirements_file_updates`, and `ci_workflow_yaml_updates`. The unchanged P02S prompt says, “Do not edit live TOML/JSON/YAML files; downstream owners apply the proven codemod,” and authorizes only codemod tooling, tests, checkpoint, and journal paths. Checkpoint v4’s reinterpretation of that sentence as merely prohibiting manual or regex edits is contrary to its plain text.

observations: P00A-B03 is resolved: the original v1 bytes are restored, the prior modified form is preserved separately, and the new corrections use v2.
Manifest v2 contains 13 completed/active entries with corrected existing paths and textually unique ownership labels.
The P00A prompt continues to validate, and working-tree changes remain within authorized planning directories.
reasoning: The history matches all four verdicts I remember issuing. I verified checkpoint v4’s digest, both manifests, restored lineage hashes, schema validation, prompt boundaries, and repository status. The lineage defect is repaired. However, restoring the original broken v1 resurrects B01 under the criterion’s explicit verification path, while the unchanged P02S prompt leaves B02 operationally unresolved.
